post.description: `wantsToHost` promotes the new account to HOST, otherwise it is a GUEST. The password is hashed with Argon2id and never returned.

201.description: The new user and the session token (also set as a cookie).

post.description: A missing email and a wrong password both return the same `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` 401, so the response never leaks which one failed.

200.description: The user and the session token (also set as a cookie).

post.summary: Log in with email and password

200.description: The user attached by the JWT guard.

302.description: Sets the session cookie and redirects to the frontend origin.
Sets the session cookie and redirects to the frontend origin.

post.description: Server-side arithmetic only: the client-sent total is never trusted (D3). Availability is decided before the price is read, so a sold-out room never leaks a price, and a room with no `room_prices` row in the requested currency is a `PRICE_UNAVAILABLE` error rather than a free stay. Writes nothing — the inventory is held when T20 writes the PENDING booking, and `holdExpiresAt` is how long the guest has to get there.

200.description: The per-night breakdown and the totals, in integer cents.

400.description: The body failed validation, or the room sleeps fewer guests than asked.

409.description: The room is sold out, blacked out, or too small for the party.

422.description: The room has no price in the requested currency.

post.summary: Price a stay and check it is bookable

post.description: Creates the PENDING booking inside a serializable transaction that re-checks availability on the transaction client before the insert, so a concurrent booking for the last unit is answered ROOM_UNAVAILABLE rather than oversold. The money is a server-computed snapshot: the request carries no money fields, and a total sent in the body is stripped, never trusted (D3). The guest contact fields are validated but not persisted — the payment flow (T26/T27) is where they live. The booking embeds a hotel display snapshot so the detail page needs no second fetch.

201.description: The PENDING booking, with its money snapshot.

400.description: The body failed validation, or the room sleeps fewer guests than asked (the 400 names the room limit).

404.description: No such room, or the room's hotel is not published.

409.description: The room is sold out, blacked out, or too small for the party (ROOM_UNAVAILABLE).

422.description: The room has no price in the requested currency.

get.description: Only the caller's own rows, newest first: the read is filtered by the JWT subject and no request field can widen it. A guest with no bookings gets an empty list, not an error.

200.description: The caller's bookings, most recent first.

get.description: 404 BOOKING_NOT_FOUND when no such booking exists; 403 NOT_BOOKING_OWNER when it exists but belongs to a different guest. The 403 rather than a 404 is deliberate: a 404 would let a caller probe whether a booking id they do not own exists.

200.description: The booking, with its hotel snapshot.

403.description: The booking exists but belongs to a different guest.

post.description: Guarded to CONFIRMED only: a PENDING booking is an unpaid hold that T26/T27 confirm, and cancelling it out from under the payment would strand the money, so a PENDING booking answers INVALID_CANCEL_STATE until it is confirmed. Refunds are a later ticket; this flips the status only. Answers 200 with the booking in its CANCELLED state, not 204: the client renders the flip from the body.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The booking to cancel, by uuid.

403.description: The booking belongs to a different guest.

409.description: The booking is not CONFIRMED (INVALID_CANCEL_STATE): PENDING until payment confirms it, and COMPLETED past cancelling.

post.description: Creates the `favorites` row for the caller. The guest is the JWT subject: a `userId` in the body is stripped by the schema, never obeyed. A hotel that is already a favourite is a `FAVORITE_EXISTS` 409 rather than a second 201, because `(userId, hotelId)` is a composite primary key and a duplicate insert is a constraint violation worth surfacing. Clients call this optimistically and roll back on the 409.

400.description: The body failed validation — `hotelId` must be a uuid.

delete.description: Always 204, including when the caller never favourited that hotel: a toggle that fails on the second click shows an error for a state the guest caused on purpose. Only the caller's own row is touched, because the row is keyed by `(userId, hotelId)` and `userId` is the JWT subject. An unknown `hotelId` is a 204 no-op too, so un-favouriting can never disagree with the toggle that called it.

parameters.name: hotelId
parameters.description: The hotel to un-favourite, by uuid.

204.description: Gone, or was never there. No body either way.

400.description: The path parameter is not a uuid.

get.description: Only PUBLISHED hotels are ever returned — the filter is in SQL, so a non-published row cannot leak through a page boundary. Prices are the cheapest room that fits `guests`, in the requested currency. Dates are accepted and validated here; availability filtering lands with the quote endpoint in T18.

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: City name, case-insensitive exact match. Omit to search every city.

parameters.name: checkIn
parameters.description: First night, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Stored as a Postgres DATE, never a timestamp.

parameters.name: checkOut
parameters.description: Last day the guest leaves, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Must be strictly after `checkIn`. The stay is half-open, so a checkout equal to another booking check-in never overlaps.

parameters.name: guests
parameters.description: Party size, 1-20. A hotel qualifies only if it has a room that fits.

parameters.name: minPrice
parameters.description: LOWEST nightly price in MAJOR currency units, not cents. `150` means 150.00. Must be <= maxPrice.

parameters.name: maxPrice
parameters.description: Highest nightly price in MAJOR currency units, not cents.

parameters.name: amenities
parameters.description: Comma-separated amenity slugs, ANDed: `wifi,pool` returns only hotels with both. Slugs are lowercase: wifi, pool, breakfast, pets, ac, workspace, gym, spa, restaurant, bar, parking, shuttle.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `recommended` (default) is star rating then name. `rating_desc` puts hotels with no reviews last, because a null average is not the best rating.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: ISO 4217 code to price in. Only USD has price rows today; a currency with no `room_prices` row yields `priceFrom: null`, never zero.

200.description: A page of hotels. `items` is empty and `total` is 0 when nothing matches.

get.description: Resolves by uuid or by slug — the frontend links to `/hotels/{slug}`. A hotel that is not PUBLISHED is a 404 for everyone but its own host, so the endpoint cannot be used to discover a draft listing.

200.description: The hotel, with rooms, amenities, images and a review summary.

404.description: No such hotel, or it is not visible to this caller.

get.description: One verdict per room, not a filtered list: the client renders a card for every room and marks the unavailable ones. A room is available when it sleeps the party AND every night has at least one unit left AND no blackout covers that night — a room at exact fit is NOT available, because the last unit taken leaves nothing to sell. A `PENDING` booking holds inventory exactly like a `CONFIRMED` one, since that is how a guest checkout holds a room before payment.

parameters.name: checkIn
parameters.description: First night, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Required: without a range there are no nights to report on, and an empty range would make every room vacuously available.

parameters.name: checkOut
parameters.description: Last day the guest leaves, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Must be strictly after `checkIn`. The stay is half-open, so `checkOut` is not one of its nights and a checkout equal to another booking's check-in never overlaps.

parameters.name: guests
parameters.description: Party size, 1-20. A room that cannot sleep the party reports `available: false` even when it has units left on every night.

200.description: Every room of the hotel, each with `available` and the units left on each night.

404.description: No such hotel, or it is not visible to this caller.

get.summary: Per-room availability for a date range

get.description: Always 200. `status` is "ok" only when the database answered; `db` carries reachability on its own, so a monitor can alert on it without parsing a status string.

200.description: The service answered. The database may still be down — read `db`.

info.title: Booking API
info.description: Hotel booking platform. Every response uses one envelope: { success: true, data } or { success: false, error: { code, message, details? } }. Branch on error.code, never on error.message.

slug.description: Stable, URL-safe. The detail route accepts this.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code the prices are quoted in.

totalInventory.description: Units the hotel sells of this room type.

remainingPerNight.description: Units left on each night, in stay order from `checkIn`. Length is `nights`. A blacked-out or fully booked night is 0; the value never goes negative.

priceCents.description: Integer cents for this night. Never major units.

feesCents.description: Zero today; T20/T26 set the real fee schedule.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code the room is priced in.

holdExpiresAt.description: ISO 8601 instant by which T20 would take the hold. A quote holds nothing by itself, so this is advisory until the booking exists.

hotelId.description: The hotel to favourite, by uuid.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 instant the favourite was created.

CreateBooking~__schema0.description: The room to book, by uuid.

CreateBooking~__schema1.description: First night, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Stored as a Postgres DATE, never a timestamp.

CreateBooking~__schema2.description: Last day the guest leaves, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Strictly after `checkIn`. The stay is half-open, so a checkout equal to another booking check-in never overlaps.

CreateBooking~__schema3.description: Party size, 1-20. Checked against the room again server-side.

CreateBooking~__schema4.description: Lead guest name. Validated, not persisted (T26/T27 consume it).

CreateBooking~__schema5.description: Lead guest email. Validated, not persisted (T26/T27 consume it).

CreateBooking~__schema6.description: Lead guest phone. Validated, not persisted (T26/T27 consume it).

CreateBooking~__schema7.description: ISO 4217 code to book in. Defaults to the room's price currency, else USD; a room with no `room_prices` row in that currency is a PRICE_UNAVAILABLE error, never a free stay.

reference.description: Human-readable, e.g. GB-4821. Shown to the guest; never the primary key.

nights.description: `checkOut - checkIn` in whole days. The stay is half-open.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code the booking was priced in. A historical label, not a key.

subtotalCents.description: Integer cents for the stay, before fees.

feesCents.description: Zero today; T20/T26 set the real fee schedule.

coverImage.description: The hotel cover image URL, or null when it has none.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 instant the booking was created.

total.description: Always `items.length` until the list is paginated.
